title: Similarity Stack / Retrieval + Rerank Architecture Discovery
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (VPC) tradeoffs
summary: Early-stage discovery for building a similarity/retrieval pipeline with reranking. Customer evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for latency-sensitive product search. Main concerns: embedding dims, vector DB choice, index recall vs latency, throughput targets, multi-tenant data isolation, and audit/KMS requirements. Agreed next step: run a small benchmark with sample dataset and share security pack and pricing for Dedicated pilot.

Schedule 30m technical PoC kickoff (tentative: 2025-11-27 with SE)
AE to send draft pricing for 3-month Dedicated pilot

transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-18 14:30 PT | Duration: 52m | Auto-recorded by Fireflies
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Marquez (Redwood SE), Lina Park (CTO, SageLens), Marcus O'Neil (Lead ML Eng), Priya Sharma (Platform Eng), Tom (Product)

[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Lina, Marcus, do you want to quickly state goals for the call?
[00:06] Lina: Yeah thanks, quick context: SageLens is building an enterprise search product for investor research, low-latency, high-recall, and we need reranking. We're evaluating how to integrate embeddings into our stack and whether to run on Redwood Hosted, get Dedicated capacity, or go Private in our VPC.
[00:22] Marcus: Our key numbers: median query latency target < 120ms for tail-sensitive flows, bursts up to 400 qps, and daily indexing of ~200k docs. Currently prototyping with pgvector but we see recall drop with higher dims and cost.
[00:36] Diego: okay, good color. Are you using off-the-shelf embeddings today? Which model and dims?
[00:41] Marcus: Right now using openai text-embedding-3-small (1536 dim) in dev but expensive. We also tried a 768-d model; quality slightly worse for our rerank step. Also experimenting with hybrid rerank where ANN returns top-k then BERT-style cross-attention reranker.
[00:56] Avery: sounds typical. A couple of clarifying questions: who owns infra—do you prefer managed vs customer-managed keys? And what's your SLA expectation?
[01:03] Lina: Platform team owns infra; security must approve KMS/HSM usage, SOC2 compliance required. SLA TBD but want predictable throughput, hence looking at Dedicated.
[01:16] Tom: On product side, we need high precision on top-5, but recall in top-100 matters for analytics. So hybrid search is attractive.
[01:28] Diego: On the hybrid design, typical pattern is embed->ANN (FAISS/HNSW/pgvector) to get top_n then lightweight reranker using a cross-encoder model. For throughput you can scale the ANN layer independently; reranker can be CPU/GPU depending on latency needs. Are you planning rerank per query or async re-scoring?
[01:45] Marcus: Real-time rerank—customers expect immediate improved ordering. So we need rerank latency ~50-80ms at 95th while ANN lookup < 20ms.
[01:54] Priya: That seems tight. Our infra currently runs on k8s with a mix of CPU nodes and 2x A100 pooled for model serving. We need guidance on efficient batching and caching—prefix caching or kv cache for conversational state.
[02:11] Avery: Redwood has a couple levers: optimized kernels, KV cache for autoregressive models, and for retrieval use we recommend separating vector store from rerank. For Hosted we handle model infra and index management; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with throughput SLOs and private networks; Private gives full control in your VPC.
[02:29] Marcus: Any recommendations on dim size? We see 1536 gives better semantic separation but costs more for storage and index build time.
[02:36] Diego: It's a tradeoff—higher dim can yield better recall but increases index memory and ANN recall tuning complexity. In practice we see 768-1024 hits a good balance for many corpora; also consider quantization (8-bit) and product-specific fine-tuning of embeddings.
[02:51] Lina: How does Redwood handle vector DB integrations—do you manage FAISS indexes or connect to external vector DBs?
[02:57] Diego: Redwood can run endpoints that either use in-house FAISS-backed indexes in the runtime or connect to your external vector DB through connectors. For Dedicated/Pvt we often colocate FAISS/Annoy/HNSW on same machines or allow you to keep a managed Milvus/Pinecone/Weaviate cluster and we route queries. There's slight latency overhead for networked vector DBs.
[03:16] Marcus: So if we keep pgvector in Postgres, what's the expected QPS?
[03:21] Diego: Pgvector is fine for small scale but CPU-bound. For 400 qps with sub-20ms lookup you'd likely need a specialized ANN index (HNSW or IVF+PQ) on memory-optimized nodes or FAISS with GPU indexing. Pgvector on standard Postgres will struggle at that scale.
[03:36] Tom: We're also worried about cold start / index build times during nightly loads. Any suggestions?
[03:40] Diego: Incremental indexing and sharding are key. For heavy ingestion you can do background PQ/IVF reclustering and use warm indexes for serving. Dedicated nodes with SSD-backed local stores help.
[03:51] [05:00] (brief cross-talk about dataset properties and noise in investor docs)
[05:40] Marcus: Can you share typical memory footprint estimates? We have ~1M docs in final system.
[05:44] Diego: Rough rule: for HNSW, memory ~ (dim * 4 bytes * #vectors) plus graph overhead; for 1536-d, 1M vectors ~= 6GB for raw float storage + graph overhead maybe 20-30GB depending on efConstruction and connections. For quantized IVF+PQ on GPU you can get this down to 1/8 or less. We'll include a sample sizing table in the benchmark.
[06:12] Priya: On security: encryption at rest, KMS, audit logs - will you accept our KMS? we have a customer-managed AWS KMS with strict rotation policies.
[06:23] Avery: Dedicated and Private both support customer KMS/HSM integrations and syslog/audit export. We'll send over the SOC2 summary and KMS integration notes. Hosted also supports encryption at rest but using Redwood-managed keys—ok for many customers but not for regulated ones.
[06:40] Lina: Also need data residency options (EU data center).
[06:44] Avery: Noted, we have EU regions; we'll flag that in the security doc.
[07:00] Marcus: Back to rerank: what models do people use? We were considering a small cross-encoder distilled BERT, runs on CPU but faster on GPU.
[07:08] Diego: Distil-cross encoders or lightweight transformer rerankers are common. Another pattern: two-stage rerank where the first re-scoring is a cheap MLP or interaction-based dot-prod on dense features, then an expensive cross-encoder for top-5. That can preserve latency while improving top-k precision.
[07:23] Marcus: Any tooling in Redwood to orchestrate that pipeline? e.g., route a request to ANN then to reranker with fallback?
[07:29] Avery: Yes, our routing policies can do multi-hop: ANN route -> if quality below threshold then trigger cross-encoder, and fallback to cheaper model if GPU cap hit. We also provide tracing and per-route token cost breakdowns for debugging.
[07:42] Tom: Curious about cost—how do you charge for embedding storage vs per-query inference?
[07:47] Avery: Hosted is usage-based (per embedding call + per-token for generation/rerank). Dedicated is commit-based for GPU pools plus per-request compute for extra usage. We'll include a draft price sheet for a 3-month pilot.
[07:59] Lina: On the PoC scope, we'd like to test: 1) ANN recall/latency for 1M vectors at dims 768/1536, 2) rerank P95 latency under load, 3) end-to-end cost estimate.
[08:12] Diego: Perfect. For the benchmark we'll create a harness that runs your queries at varying QPS, measures ANN recall (using your relevance labels), and runs reranker with different batch sizes. We'll also try FAISS on GPU vs HNSW on CPU and quantify tradeoffs.
[08:26] Marcus: What's the expected engineering effort to spin up Dedicated vs Private?
[08:30] Avery: Dedicated is fastest—reserved capacity we provision and you get predictable SLO; Private (VPC) requires network setup, IAM/KMS setup, and we do an on-prem or VPC install which could take a few weeks depending on compliance checks.
[08:42] Priya: We might prefer Dedicated for pilot and then move to Private if controls demand it.
[08:46] Avery: Many customers do the same.
[09:00] [09:12] (Diego shares screen briefly — notes about benchmark config, sample command lines; brief audio glitch, 'Redwood Dedicate' mis-transcribed in the notes)
[09:45] Diego: Example FAISS GPU command for IVF+PQ and PQ bits — we'll test 8-bit quantization and PQ 16 subquantizers; expect memory reduction but tune for recall.
[09:58] Marcus: When you mention PQ, how does that affect rerank? If ANN returns compressed vectors, will reranker quality drop because scores not exact?
[10:06] Diego: Typically you use PQ for ANN retrieval only; you store full-precision vectors for rerank or store doc embeddings and re-embed content for cross-encoder. The ANN top-k will be approximated but reranker operates on original text or higher-fidelity embeddings.
[10:20] Tom: Are there built-in connectors for Pinecone/Milvus?
[10:24] Avery: We have connectors and customers often use them. For the lowest latency and control we recommend colocated FAISS or a Managed Milvus on Dedicated. We'll include connectors doc link in the follow-up.
[10:36] Lina: Any compliance pitfalls we've missed? e.g., logs that might leak sensitive PII, retention windows?
[10:41] Avery: Good point—retention controls, redaction, and masking are options. We'll show how audit logs can be filtered. For HIPAA/financial data, Private deployments are common to meet strict controls.
[10:56] Marcus: Timing question: we want a 6-week pilot. What's realistic?
[11:00] Avery: For a focused pilot with Dedicated capacity, 4-6 weeks is reasonable: week 1 provision + baseline, weeks 2-3 run benchmarks and iterate, weeks 4-6 integrate and validate. Private will add lead time.
[11:12] Priya: Cost sensitivity—if we commit to Dedicated do we get lower per-query rates?
[11:17] Avery: Yes, committed capacity reduces unit cost and gives predictable throughput. We'll add example numbers in the pricing sheet.
[11:25] Marcus: Can the reranker be hosted on Redwood but index kept in our VPC? We want data control for vectors.
[11:33] Diego: Yes — hybrid deployment: you can keep vector DB inside your VPC and route rerank requests to Redwood endpoints, with mTLS and private peering. Some network latency exists but often acceptable.
[11:45] Tom: Do you support query-time feature enrichment? e.g., include metadata signals in reranker?
[11:50] Diego: Absolutely—rerankers can consume dense vectors + structured signals (timestamps, popularity) as features. We recommend normalizing those during ingestion.
[12:00] [12:10] (short pause; participant network jitter)
[12:32] Lina: Ok let's recap and assign owners.
[12:35] Avery: Recap: Redwood to send security pack + EU region notes; Diego to produce benchmark harness and recommended FAISS/HNSW configs for dims 768 & 1536; Marcus to provide sample dataset and query labels; schedule PoC kickoff.
[12:49] Marcus: Sounds good. One last Q: for 1M vectors, if we choose 1024 dim, what's rough cost footprint?
[12:55] Diego: We'll include cost sensitivity table; rough rule-of-thumb storage + memory + GPU inference for reranker will be part of the benchmark.
[13:05] Avery: Great—thanks all. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the PoC kickoff and attach the docs.
[13:11] Tom: Thanks everyone.
[13:13] (meeting ended)
